Messages.Author: Daniel Jocham
Messages.Body:
I do have two questions.

1.) Sabbat Vampire cannot become Princes etc and vice versa.
But if a Camarilla vampire calls a referendum to become prince, can Sabbat
titleholders VOTE? It doesnt make very much sense...

2.) I had an argument with a friend of mine about the anouncement of
additional strikes in a combat. According to the V:tES Complete Rules
Reference (v2.12) each minion resolve his normal strike, and THEN the
minions get the possibility to gain additional strikes. My friend argues,
that its not possible to play cards after damage prevention. He states, that
additional strikes has to be announced after establishing range when the
strikes are choosen.

Thanks in advance.
--
Daniel Jocham alias dan...@sbox.tu-graz.ac.at

Messages.Author: Lupus Australis
Messages.Body:
On 28 Aug 1998, Daniel Jocham wrote:

> I do have two questions.
>
> 1.) Sabbat Vampire cannot become Princes etc and vice versa.
> But if a Camarilla vampire calls a referendum to become prince, can Sabbat
> titleholders VOTE? It doesnt make very much sense...

Yes they can. You can, however, play "Closed Session" to prevent them
from doing this.

It does not make sense if taken literally, but you do not have to take it
literally by assuming that Sabbat vampires vote openly in the Camarilla.
There are other ways you can rationalize their influence on the political
process.

Once you accept that the game contains vampires from more than one sect,
you must accept that the voting process can no longer be considered merely
an internal affair to a given sect. When a vampire calls a Praxis
Siezure, he is not merely siezing power within the Camarilla, but within
all of vampiredom, and within the Jyhad as a whole. To the extent that
this is true (and lets assume that it is true for all vampires in this
particular skirmish within the Jyhad) then influential vampires within
other sects may have means to prevent this from happening.

Lupus Australis

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Daniel Jocham wrote:
> 1.) Sabbat Vampire cannot become Princes etc and vice versa.
> But if a Camarilla vampire calls a referendum to become prince, can Sabbat
> titleholders VOTE?

Yes.

> 2.) I had an argument with a friend of mine about the anouncement of
> additional strikes in a combat. According to the V:tES Complete Rules
> Reference (v2.12) each minion resolve his normal strike, and THEN the
> minions get the possibility to gain additional strikes. My friend argues,
> that its not possible to play cards after damage prevention. He states, that
> additional strikes has to be announced after establishing range when the
> strikes are choosen.

Additional strikes are played after the initial strike resolution
(resolution of the first pair of strikes). Or as specified on
card text, of course (Vial of Garou blood, Acrobatics, etc.)

Messages.Author: Mark Langsdorf
Messages.Body:
Daniel Jocham wrote in message <6s5r73$r...@fstgal00.tu-graz.ac.at>...

>I do have two questions.
>

>1.) Sabbat Vampire cannot become Princes etc and vice versa.
>But if a Camarilla vampire calls a referendum to become prince, can Sabbat

>titleholders VOTE? It doesnt make very much sense...

Sure it does. The Archbishop of Mexico City leaks the word that
if Smudge becomes the Prince of Dallas, then there's going to be a big
Crusade on Dallas within the week. The Primogen of Dallas promptly
inform Smudge that he's going to be Ignored on this one.
Similarly, when Roy tries to become the Archbishop of New York,
Gilbert Duane casually mentions that it'd be a real shame if some
of those muddled vampire hunters he knew got a list of all the prominent
Sabbat in New York and a couple of flamethrowers, so Roy goes out
on his ear.
It's not like vampire meet at parliment over tea to call votes, you
know?
